answer.text: The monetary value of a society's physical infrastructure
Networks together with shared norms, values and understandings that facilitate cooperation within or among groups
The GDP of a country divided by population
The total sum of philanthropic capital raised in a given year

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 1.5.1 (iii), the OECD defines Social Capital as 'networks together with shared norms, values and understandings that facilitate cooperation within or among groups'. The World Bank adds institutional and relational dimensions. The Trap: Option A confuses with physical capital. Option C is per-capita GDP. Option D confuses with philanthropic capital. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-links to Ch 4 (Logic Model) and Ch 6 (Frameworks). Social capital is a cross-cutting theme across most SAS standards. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For SAS-400 community-engagement assurance, capture social-capital proxies: self-help group formation, cooperative membership growth, trust-in-institutions Likert scores. These translate qualitative 'community cohesion' into auditable indicators.
